limits_note: a WebSocket message from an existing connection resets the 15-minute timer, which the vendor states explicitly
reliability_note: 'Render might restart a Free web service at any time'; a service that initiates an uncommonly high volume of outbound traffic may be suspended
notes: The corpus open question 'does a cron job count against the 15-minute sleep' resolves to neither: a cron job is a separate service type that cannot be on the free plan, because 'There is a minimum monthly charge of $1 per cron job service.' Its executions also run in a separate container from the web service and do not keep it awake. What is still unverified is whether a spun-down service wakes purely from an inbound request to a non-HTTP port; the docs name only HTTP requests and new WebSocket connections.

free_tier.stated: A Free web service with an ephemeral filesystem, 750 Free instance hours per workspace per calendar month, and a 5 GB monthly outbound bandwidth allowance on the Hobby plan.

retention.stated: the filesystem is ephemeral and is lost on every redeploy, restart or spin-down; a Free Postgres database expires 30 days after creation

egress.terms: Hobby workspaces include 5 GB of outbound bandwidth a month, then USD 0.15 per GB; without a payment method Render suspends all Free services for the rest of the month

identity_cost.detail: an account is enough for a Free web service; a payment method is optional and its absence converts a bandwidth overrun into a suspension instead of a bill
